title: Pakistan Army 275th Corps Commanders' Conference: Asim Munir Chairs Marka-e-Haq Anniversary Session — 'Nation Stands United, Resilient, and Fully Prepared'
detail: Field Marshal Asim Munir chaired the 275th Corps Commanders' Conference at GHQ Rawalpindi on May 5, 2026 — two days before the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor (May 7, 2025), which Pakistan calls 'Marka-e-Haq.' The conference formally congratulated the nation and armed forces on the anniversary, declaring that 'national commemoration of Marka-e-Haq serves as a clear message to the Indian hubristic political mindset that the Pakistani nation stands united, resilient, and fully prepared.' Key outcomes: (1) Regional peace and stability were linked to 'collective restraint, responsibility, and respect for sovereignty' — a signal directed at India ahead of the anniversary; (2) The forum 'strongly condemned ongoing atrocities, extrajudicial killings, and demographic changes in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK),' reaffirming Pakistan's 'continued diplomatic, political, and moral support for the Kashmiri people'; (3) Munir directed commanders to 'maintain the highest levels of vigilance, operational readiness, and adaptability'; (4) Counter-terrorism operations and Afghan Taliban policies were reviewed. The Corps Commanders' Conference — Pakistan Army's apex operational coordination body — convening specifically on the Marka-e-Haq anniversary week signals that Pakistan's military establishment is using the first anniversary as both an internal cohesion exercise and an outward messaging operation. The conference's language directly responds to India's anniversary narrative: where India frames Sindoor as a voluntary halt ('we stopped on our own terms — Rajnath Singh), Pakistan frames Marka-e-Haq as a defensive victory that proved Pakistani resolve. The Rawalpindi session occurred simultaneously with India's ongoing Shaurya Defence Technology Symposium (May 4–6), producing sharply competing narratives with one day remaining before May 7.

media.caption: Pakistan's 275th Corps Commanders' Conference chaired by Field Marshal Asim Munir at GHQ Rawalpindi (May 5, 2026): military top brass congratulates nation on Marka-e-Haq anniversary

title: Pakistan FM Dar Briefs Full Diplomatic Corps on Marka-e-Haq Anniversary: 'No Compromise on Sovereignty' — Countering India's Rajnath Narrative
detail: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar formally briefed the full Diplomatic Corps accredited to Pakistan on May 5, 2026 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Islamabad, as part of Pakistan's official marking of the first anniversary of 'Marka-e-Haq' — Pakistan's name for the May 7–10, 2025 confrontation. Dar characterized Marka-e-Haq as 'a historic moment when Pakistan's armed forces, backed by the people, defended Pakistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity against unprovoked Indian aggression.' He underscored 'no compromise on sovereignty' while reiterating commitment to 'dialogue and diplomacy.' The diplomatic briefing — with ambassadors and high commissioners from across the world present — is a significant escalation of Pakistan's international outreach, designed to embed Pakistan's official narrative of the May 2025 conflict into diplomatic channels ahead of the anniversary. Pakistan's official framing presents the confrontation as: (1) defensive — Pakistan responded to 'unprovoked Indian aggression'; (2) sovereign — Pakistan acted within its legitimate rights; (3) diplomatically managed — Pakistan secured an internationally supported ceasefire. The briefing directly counters India's own anniversary messaging: Rajnath Singh's statements calling Sindoor a 'voluntary halt' and Pakistan's nuclear threats a 'bluff' (April 30), and his Shaurya Symposium speeches calling it a 'golden chapter' (May 4). By briefing the Diplomatic Corps on May 5, Pakistan has now taken the anniversary narrative to an international audience one day before the anniversary. No Indian government response to the specific diplomatic briefing was reported.

media.caption: FM Ishaq Dar briefs the full Diplomatic Corps at MoFA Islamabad on the Marka-e-Haq anniversary (May 5, 2026): 'No compromise on sovereignty — Pakistan acted in self-defense'
